normalized.governing_thought: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro tier at +$12 per seat, with a usage allowance, and make the mobile rewrite the next commitment
executive_summary: Launch? Yes, in Q2 2027. Routewise has bundled AI scheduling since Sept 2026, and our win rate against them fell from 44% to 37%. Holding back costs up to ~$1.1M ARR a year in lost deals and AI churn. The price is a two-quarter delay to the mobile rewrite, which is a real cost (slide 8).

Packaging: Include Copilot in a new Pro plan; no standalone add-on. This matches how Routewise sells AI. It also ties price to account size: a 3-seat shop pays $36 a month, not $149. And it avoids an add-on that mostly attracts the heaviest users.

Price: Pro = Core + $12 per seat per month ($91), with 600 AI requests per seat per month pooled; overage $20 per 1,000. The allowance keeps company gross margin at or above 75% even if every Pro account uses Copilot heavily.

Value: $1.2M–$2.9M expansion ARR in year one (14–33% of accounts move to Pro). That adds +2.1 to +5.0 NRR points. The CPO's $8M is not supported: only 14% of beta accounts bought at $149, against the 46% who said they would in the survey.

NRR 105%: Copilot alone is unlikely to get there; Copilot plus the mobile rewrite does, even in the low case. Mobile reliability drives 27% of churn, against 6% for AI. The 14 engineers go back to mobile as soon as Copilot launches.

Guardrails: Review at end of Q3 2027: ≥8% of accounts on Pro, inference cost ≤$5.40 per Pro seat, win rate against Routewise recovering, productivity gains holding outside the volunteer accounts, and the mobile rewrite restarted. Renegotiate the inference contract before Dec 2027.

Engineering cost: 14 engineers × 0.5 year × $210,000 = $1.47M

Mobile fix NRR effect: 50% of mobile churn retained ÷ $57.6M (illustrative) = +1.9 pts
Company gross margin: (ARR + uplift − 22% × ARR − inference − $0.6M) ÷ (ARR + uplift) — see slides 6, 10

normalized.recommendation: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro tier at +$12 per seat, with a usage allowance, and make the mobile rewrite the next commitment. alternatives_considered.option: A. Hold: mobile first, no Copilot
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected. $0 expansion ARR, 0 NRR pts (mobile helps later); keeps losing AI-led deals and AI churn; mobile rewrite on time. Delaying Copilot loses up to ≈ $0.6M for good (new deals $0.3M + AI churn $0.25M) and pushes back $1.2–2.9M of Pro expansion. 'A close call on the numbers'; launching favoured because Routewise is already selling AI and expansion is the only lever with a fast NRR effect.

Rejected. $1.2M–$2.5M expansion ARR (not $8.1M), +2.1 to +4.3 NRR pts, $0.1M–$0.8M contribution; gross-margin risk unbounded (heavy users buy; top 10% leave 12% margin); AI costs extra so we look pricier vs Routewise; $149 is 63% on top of a 3-seat bill; mobile delayed 2 quarters. 'the $149 add-on earns no more'.

Recommended. $1.2M–$2.9M expansion ARR, +2.1 to +5.0 NRR pts, $0.2M–$1.3M contribution; margin risk bounded (≥55% on uplift at the allowance); like-for-like packaging vs Routewise; 3 seats pay $36 a month; mobile delayed 2 quarters.
Rejected implicitly on slide 6: uncapped, every account at paywall-buyer usage would push company GM to 74.1%, a breach of the 75% floor.

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck contains no pictures; charts came through as extracted series values (shown as they appear, e.g. 1.9255 and 0.641834 for $M, and fractions for percentages). On slide 9 the stacked chart has 'base' and 'value' series that make up a waterfall; the axis starts at 98%. Slide 13's numbering is irregular (items 1, 2, an unnumbered item, 3, blank 4, 5, 6), so I listed the decisions in the order they appear. Slide 2's executive-summary labels ('Launch?', 'Packaging', etc.) are kept as prefixes on each point. On slide 6, the left-hand narrative column was split into separate claims. In alternatives_considered, two entries are not columns in the options table on slide 7: the 'Pro uncapped' option comes from the slide 6 table, and the 'lower uplift' fallback comes from the slide 12 guardrails.
